ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, we know for the rectangle $ABCD$, where $AD=10$ and $AB=6$. Now, the side $AD$ is rotated about one of its endpoints, and when the other endpoint falls exactly at point E on the line where side $BC$ is located, what is the length of the segment $DE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure,\\
$\because$ The quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle,\\
$\therefore$ AB=CD=6, AD=BC=10, $\angle$ABC=$\angle$DCB=$90^\circ$,\\
When AD=AE=10, BE= $\sqrt{AE^{2}-AB^{2}}=\sqrt{10^{2}-6^{2}}=8$,\\
$\therefore$ DE$_{1}$= $\sqrt{CD^{2}+EC^{2}}=\sqrt{6^{2}+2^{2}}=2\sqrt{10}$, DE$_{2}$= $\sqrt{CD^{2}+EC^{2}}=\sqrt{6^{2}+18^{2}}=6\sqrt{10}$,\\
When DE=DA=10, DE=10,\\
In summary, the values of DE that meet the conditions are $\boxed{2\sqrt{10}}$, $\boxed{6\sqrt{10}}$, or $\boxed{10}$.
